flags.evidence: Opened page/index.html from disk (file://, no network, no page errors) in Chromium at 1440x900 and 390x844 and scrolled to section #review, headed 'Written for the person who has to approve it'. At both widths the yellow-ruled paragraph p.aside-note below the three points is visible (display block, opacity 1; 18px at 1440, 17px at 390) and reads: 'For the sales engineer waiting on all this: a draft that arrives already checked gets approved in one pass instead of three. The speed comes from fewer rounds, not from skipping the review.' 'One pass instead of three' is a quantified savings/performance claim (review rounds cut from three to one) stated as fact. It is outside the demo, and nothing in #review labels it as an example, sample or illustration. The brief says there are 'no accuracy or time-saved numbers', and the page itself says in #pilot that it has no time-saved figures. The 'Does not count' column does not cover it: it is not a brief fact, it is not labelled sample data inside the demo, and it is not a plain status statement. This meets the HF2 'Counts' definition (usage, performance, accuracy or savings numbers not supplied by the brief and presented as fact).
